html:
Mesoamerican peoples made rubber from the latex of the rubber tree and played a ritual ball game with it for some 3,000 years, from about 1650 BCE. They mixed the latex with the juice of a morning glory vine, which made it tough and bouncy, long before rubber was known in Europe.

The oldest known ball court, at Paso de la Amada on the Pacific coast of Chiapas, dates to about 1650 BCE. Solid rubber balls from about 1600 BCE were found in a bog at El Manatí, in Olmec country. Players hit the heavy ball mainly with their hips.

Almost every later city had a court, from Monte Albán to Chichen Itza and Tenochtitlan. The game was sport, gambling and religion at once, and some games ended in human sacrifice. In the Popol Vuh, the Hero Twins play ball against the lords of the underworld. A form of the game, ulama, is still played in Sinaloa, Mexico.
